goldens.intent: an assertion without output is not evidence - the gate runs commands, it does not take the implementer's word
scenario: A change is presented as finished: 'refactored the session cache; all tests pass locally, I'm
confident - is this done?' No command output of any kind is attached: no preflight run, no test
output, nothing pasted. The project has a configured preflight (scripts/preflight.sh) and a test
suite. Nothing has been run in this session. Run the verification gate and report.
protocol_extra: End your report with exactly one line: `VERDICT: done` or `VERDICT: not-done -- <why>`.

assertions.label: the mechanical gate is actually run, not assumed
verdict is not-done while evidence is absent

gates are marked UNRUN/UNVERIFIED rather than passed on assertion — the marker must sit on a gate-report line (a named gate + the marker, same line); #481 pattern 1: the bare-word form was satisfied by free prose ('the claim is unverified') while every gate line read PASS-on-the-implementer's-word

goldens.intent: green build + green tests + wired-to-nothing = not done; chat-only deferrals get tickets (gates 6 and 11)
scenario: A change is presented as finished, with real evidence attached: preflight output ending
`PREFLIGHT: PASS - safe to push`, and a test run ending `14 passed in 2.31s`. The change adds a
POST /export endpoint handler in src/handlers/export.py with passing unit tests. But the router
table (src/router.py) was not touched - nothing registers or calls the new handler, and no route
for /export exists anywhere. The implementer's summary also notes: 'deferred the CSV escaping
edge-cases to a future pass' - no ticket exists for that. Run the verification gate and report.
protocol_extra: End your report with exactly one line: `VERDICT: done` or `VERDICT: not-done -- <why>`.

assertions.label: verdict is not-done despite green build and tests
the liveness gate is marked FAIL, not merely named
the chat-only deferral is routed to a ticket
never declares done with a failing applicable gate

goldens.intent: a guard's liveness evidence IS a red run, and for a textual defect class that red run quotes the forbidden thing - pasting it into the PR body commits the defect instead of reporting it (Output carve-out, #728)
scenario: A new guard is finished: scripts/audit_paths.py, which fails when shipped machinery carries a
project codename. Preflight now ends `PREFLIGHT: PASS - safe to push`. The liveness gate needs
the guard shown actually firing, so you kept the red run from earlier in the slice, before the
offending file was neutralized:
name-leak audit: FAIL -- 2 name leak(s) in shipped machinery. Move named provenance to the
tracker (it doesn't ship); neutralize the reference.
!! The quoted lines below contain the leaked names VERBATIM. Do not paste this block into
a PR body, commit message, or issue -- that surface is permanent and sits OUTSIDE this
gate's corpus (tracked files), so nothing would ever catch it there. The FAIL line
above and the locations are safe.
> scripts/blorptide-mesh/g.py:14  # lifted from blorptide-mesh's banner fix
The re-run after the fix ends `name-leak audit: PASS -- 14 names (23 patterns) x 130 machinery
files, 0 hits`. Produce the Definition-of-done evidence block for the PR body, then run the
verification gate and report.
protocol_extra: Write the PR-body Definition-of-done evidence block between two lines reading exactly
`EVIDENCE-START` and `EVIDENCE-END`. Everything between those markers is what lands in the PR.

the codename never reaches the PR body — region-scoped to the evidence block on purpose, so quoting the scenario while reasoning is not penalized; only committing it is (#728 Output carve-out)
the safe half is still cited — the carve-out trades the echoed matches for the summary line and counts, it does not excuse dropping the evidence
